key_insight: A complex foundation model for zero-shot dynamical-system reconstruction can be reduced to a minimal two-parameter, interpretable linear blend that still performs competitively across chaotic and cyclic systems.
engineering_relevance: This suggests highly lightweight, analytically tractable models may be sufficient for deployment when the goal is out-of-domain dynamical reconstruction rather than full black-box forecasting.
method: Iteratively simplify the SOTA DynaMix architecture into DynaBase.
Forecast by blending the current latent state with the nearest in-context neighbor and its temporal successor.
Derive closed-form one-step prediction behavior and optimize directly for reconstruction metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive zero-shot reconstruction across chaotic and cyclic dynamical systems, with parameter counts many orders of magnitude below other foundation models.
watch_item: The extreme simplicity likely makes performance sensitive to how in-context neighbors are selected and may trade off short-term prediction optimality against reconstruction quality.
paper_title: A Minimal Interpretable Architecture for Zero-Shot Reconstruction of Dynamical Systems
